00_title.text:
an open-source research workspace for testing
momentum rotation strategies on Indian equities.

In the next few minutes, I'll show
you what it does, how to set it up,
and how to write and test your first alpha.

01_why.text: Most backtests are optimistic by accident.

They use today's index members, fill
at the close that produced the signal,
and treat charges as a footnote.
This lab makes those choices explicit.

membership is applied as of each
rebalance date from official snapshots.
After 2022 those are irregular official anchors,
with coverage between them marked unknown.

The command line records the universe
label, but does not re-filter.

A signal formed on the close of day
T can only fill at the open of T+1.
Every trade pays brokerage, STT, exchange fees,
Stamp duty is charged on buys only,

and the rates are 2026-style
constants, not the historical schedule.

02_pipeline.text:
A private, checksummed data pack
supplies split-and-bonus-adjusted bars.

The research harness joins
point-in-time membership to them.

The full point-in-time NIFTY 500 membership
chain behind the headline is not public.

The canonical engine ranks
trailing returns, holds the top N,
and executes at the next open.
The research report adds beta, Jensen's alpha,

Newey-West t-statistics, and a
block-bootstrap p-value for the headline.

The 968-row table carries beta,
alpha, and both t-statistics,
And all 968 sweep rows are published,
including the rows that say no.

03_setup.text:
Setup is quick if you only
want the code and tests.

Clone the repository, sync with
uv, and run the test suite.
The suite is offline and needs no data pack.

For the research UI, install the
lab extra and launch Streamlit.

Its pack detector does not yet
recognise the 1.0.0 layout,
so use the CLI for a real pack.

To run a real backtest, request
access to the private pack, verify it,

then point the command line
at it with NSE_DATA_DIR,
or by placing it in the local data directory.

Verification refuses to
continue on a hash mismatch.

04_spec.text: An alpha here is a specification, not a class.

You label the universe, declare
the holding count, the lookback,
the cadence, and any exit overlay.

The spec is explicit; charge rates
and starting cash are fixed constants.

An unknown field is an error,
never silently ignored.
This is the pre-specified primary: NIFTY 500,

the top 10 by 63-session momentum,
monthly cadence, next-open fills,

The published run rebalances
on membership evidence dates,

so after 2022 it is event-anchored
rather than strictly monthly.

05_run.text: Run one spec with the backtest command.

The command line runs the engine
over the bars in the pack.

The published study applies point-in-time
membership in its research harness.

You get sessions, rebalances,
trades, skips, final cash,

Add the out flag, and the full equity
curve, every trade, every exit,
and every skip are written as JSON.

The run in this shot uses
a small synthetic pack,

so you can see the mechanics
without the 161 MB data pack.

It is labelled synthetic on screen,
and it is not a research result.

06_test.text:
Targeted tests pin the engine's causality
and accounting: next-open fills,
The full suite runs offline on frozen fixtures.

A separate validation harness
records 348 fail-closed checks,

including 36 independent recomputations
of beta, alpha, tracking error,

The rest are contract and
CSV consistency checks.

The last published run records
348 checks, 0 failures.

The harness checks every published
row's accounting identities,

cross checks the six headline
rows against the published CSV,

and recomputes the alpha
regressions from aligned returns.

On the benchmark-aligned sessions

08_outro.text:
The tutorial, architecture notes,
the full 968-row results table,
and the disclaimer are in the repository.

The study's JSON inputs and
verification payload are not public,

so read What is reproducible
before you try to rerun it.
If you use it, cite it.
And remember, this is research software.

and past performance does
not predict future returns.
